displayedInputs.question: What is the ones digit of \[\begin{align*} & 222,222 - 22,222 - 2,222 \\ &- 222 - 22 - 2? \end{align*}\]
What is the value of this expression in decimal form? \[ \frac{44}{11} + \frac{110}{44} + \frac{44}{1100} \]
When Yunji added all the integers from \(1\) to \(9,\) she mistakenly left out a number. Her incorrect sum turned out to be a square number. Which number did Yunji leave out?
Aaliyah rolls two standard \(6\)-sided dice. She notices that the product of the two numbers rolled is a multiple of \(6.\) Which of the following integers cannot be the sum of the two numbers?

On Monday Taye has \(\$2.\) Every day, he either gains \(\$3\) or doubles the amount of money he had on the previous day. How many different dollar amounts could Taye have on Thursday, \(3\) days later?

All of the marbles in Maria’s collection are red, green, or blue. Maria has half as many red marbles as green marbles and twice as many blue marbles as green marbles. Which of the following could be the total number of marbles in Maria’s collection?

In January \(1980\) the Mauna Loa Observatory recorded carbon dioxide CO\({}_{2}\) levels of \(338\) ppm (parts per million). Over the years the average CO\({}_{2}\) reading has increased by about \(1.515\) ppm each year. What is the expected CO\({}_{2}\) level in ppm in January \(2030?\) Round your answer to the nearest integer.

Rohan keeps a total of \(90\) guppies in \(4\) fish tanks.

• There is \(1\) more guppy in the \(2\)nd tank than in the \(1\)st tank.

• There are \(2\) more guppies in the \(3\)rd tank than in the \(2\)nd tank.

• There are \(3\) more guppies in the \(4\)th tank than in the \(3\)rd tank.

How many guppies are in the \(4\)th tank?

Let the letters \(F,\) \(L,\) \(Y,\) \(B,\) \(U,\) \(G\) represent distinct digits. Suppose \(\text{FLYFLY}\) is the greatest number that satisfies the equation \[ 8 \cdot \text{FLYFLY} = \text{BUGBUG}. \] What is the value of \(\text{FLY} + \text{BUG}?\)

Minh enters the numbers \(1\) through \(81\) into the cells of a \(9 \times 9\) grid in some order. She calculates the product of the numbers in each row and column. What is the least number of rows and columns that could have a product divisible by \(3?\)

mappings.answerReason: Let a = FLY and b = BUG. Since the repeated numbers are 1001a and 1001b, b = 8a ≤ 999, so a ≤ 124. The candidate 124 gives 992, which repeats 9. The next candidate 123 gives 984 with six distinct digits, so the requested sum is 123 + 984 = 1107.

routes.label: Check integer row and column capacities

mappings.rationale: A row or column qualifies exactly when it contains a multiple of 3. The 27 such entries must fit within the intersections of the affected rows and columns. Prove a universal capacity bound and construct an arrangement attaining it.
mappings.answerReason: There are 27 multiples of 3 among 1 through 81. If they occupy r rows and c columns, then rc ≥ 27. A total r + c ≤ 10 would give rc ≤ 25, which is impossible. Conversely, place the 27 multiples in 27 cells of a 4 × 7 rectangle and fill all remaining cells with nonmultiples. Exactly 4 rows and 7 columns then qualify, attaining 11.
